payload.text: Paper finding INV-M (docs/truth-ledger-paper-v2.md, Appendix A): a claim's --paths can be filed as a glob that matches zero tracked files -- most concretely, space-separated paths ('a.sh b.sh') silently store as one literal path matching nothing. The claim's hash still matches, a verifier still agrees, and the invalidation trigger can never fire -- the protection is decorative. Not hypothetical here: tr-3591aae0 hit exactly this (evidence_paths stored as a single space-joined string), found by inspection, retracted, superseded by tr-94a98135 with correct comma-separated paths. Currently mitigated only by the operating convention (file a successor, retract the original), not a gate. Fix (already scoped in the paper): an intake check refusing (a) whitespace-containing path entries with no comma, and (b) any path/glob that matches zero tracked files at filing time; plus a canary fault seeding a dead tripwire and asserting the new check refuses it. Lands in the truth-ledger template (scripts/truth, truth-canary.sh, ADR + paper Appendix A row for INV-M's promotion from proposed to shipped), then syncs back here via copier update, same shape as the ADR-006/F7 cycle.

payload.text: Measured on the kuchnie ledger 2026-08-04 (2168 records, 671 invalidations, 608 of them resolved by a later verdict): staling is dominated by false alarms. The fact had not changed in 530 of 608 resolved stalings, against 78 where it had -- a false:true ratio above 3:1. Within the false half, 242 were provable mechanically by an unchanged evidence hash and 288 required a human to re-read and agree, so the mechanically-healable share is under half. This reproduces Estler et al. (2014) locally: specifications change far less than implementations, and 62 percent of stalings here are triggered by implementation paths, so a high false-stale rate under a path-touched-means-stale rule is structural rather than incidental. The recipe reports the ratio BAND rather than the counts, so it diverges when the finding changes instead of whenever the ledger grows.

Re-run both ways on the same ledger: file order gives 608/242/288/78, fold order gives 630/262/293/75. The cited counts in this claim are therefore method-artifacts. The claim's CONCLUSION survives both orders -- false:true stays above 3:1 and the mechanically-healable share stays under half, which is why the band-based recipe did not catch this -- but the sentence states counts it should not. evidence.command: jq -s "sort_by(.ts, .id) | reduce .[] as \$e ({p:{},m:0,h:0,t:0}; if \$e.kind==\"invalidation\" then .p[\$e.payload.claim]=1 elif \$e.kind==\"verdict\" and (.p[\$e.payload.claim]//null)!=null then ((\$e.payload.basis//\"\")|startswith(\"reaffirm:\")) as \$m | (if \$e.payload.verdict==\"agree\" and \$m then .m+=1 elif \$e.payload.verdict==\"agree\" then .h+=1 else .t+=1 end) | .p=(.p|del(.[\$e.payload.claim])) else . end) | (.m+.h) as \$f | \"false:true=\" + (if \$f >= 3*.t then \">=3:1\" elif \$f > .t then \">1:1\" else \"<=1:1\" end) + \" auto-healed-share=\" + (if .m*2 >= \$f then \"at-least-half\" else \"under-half\" end)" .truth/claims.jsonl

payload.text: Measured on the kuchnie ledger 2026-08-04 in the kernel's canonical fold order (fold_key = ts, id, canon; ADR-016): of 630 stalings resolved by a later verdict, 555 were resolved by an agree and 75 by a diverge, retraction or cannot_verify -- a false:true ratio above 3:1, which survives a file-order walk and a reclassification of retracted and cannot_verify. Of the 555, 262 were auto-healed by the reaffirm verb and 293 carried a hand-written basis. That second figure is an UPPER bound on genuinely human work, not a measure of it: the recipe classifies by whether the reaffirm verb filed the verdict, so a dispatched verifier who ran recheck, saw the hash match, and typed an agree lands in the hand-written bucket. At least 35 of those bases say in their own words that the hash matched. The recipe therefore reports the AUTO-HEALED share, and the band it prints is to be read that way. Successor to tr-e1225a78, whose sentence named the bucket after an unchanged evidence hash while computing it from the reaffirm verb, and whose 172+100+6 breakdown omitted a fourth bucket of 15 and so failed to sum to its own 293.
